items.shortLine: Meet Neta & walk through your plan
items.detailText: Meet Neta on Day 1. You'll walk through your onboarding plan together — what to expect these first few weeks, and how the two of you will work together.
A walk around the Tel Aviv office with Tal, one of your teammates — where things are and how the space works, from someone who isn't your manager.
A self-paced session on Veridian's vision, values, departments, and the three offices — Tel Aviv, London, and Austin. First of six sessions on the company.
A short self-paced course on the security basics everyone at Veridian needs to know — due by Day 7.
A quick read on how people work together at Veridian and what's expected of everyone — due by Day 7.
Email, calendar, and shared drive — set up before you even start, so it's waiting for you on Day 1.
Slack access lands Day 1 — where the People Partners team and the managers you support communicate day to day.
Notion access is ready Day 1 — home for Veridian's People policies, playbooks, and internal HR documentation.
HiBob is ready Day 1 — the HRIS you'll work in daily on behalf of the managers you support, plus your own employee profile and time off.
No buddy assigned yet — your manager will pair you with one soon. They're your go-to for the everyday questions.
Neta walks you through the full operating picture of the People function in one sitting — mission, metrics, workflows, key interfaces, and where to find docs and reports.
Connect with a fellow HRBP on the team to compare notes on how the portfolio model works day to day.
Connect with the team's senior HRBP — a good resource once you're navigating trickier portfolio situations.
Get set up on benefits and logistics, with a direct contact at HR from here on.
A self-paced look at what Veridian builds: Knowledge Hub, AI Assistant, AI Agents, and Governance. Second of six sessions on the company.
A short course on data privacy fundamentals, required for everyone at Veridian — due by Day 14.
A self-paced session on Veridian's market and the kinds of customers it serves. Third of six sessions on the company.
A self-paced session on Veridian's business model. Fourth of six sessions on the company.
A self-paced session on the key metrics Veridian tracks. Fifth of six sessions on the company.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, and the person who runs Product — a first conversation to start building that relationship.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, on the Finance team — a chance to get a first sense of how her team works.
Stay aligned with Neta this week and flag anything that already feels off track.
A self-paced session on Veridian's strategic direction and near-term roadmap — the last of the six company sessions.
Another leader in your portfolio, on the Finance team — a name and a face before his first real ask.

items.shortLine: Say hello to Yael, your skip-level
items.detailText: Meet Yael Shalev, VP People — the leader of the whole People function you're now part of.
A quick sync with Neta this week to catch anything before it piles up.
A session with Neta on where People fits into Veridian and what it's aiming for this year.
A self-guided read through the policies that matter most day to day — hybrid work, security, and expenses.
This week's check-in doubles as your 30-day review — stepping back with Neta to see how the first month matched the plan and re-prioritize together.
The CEO, and one of the leaders in your portfolio — a chance to put a face to the name early on.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, and the person who runs Revenue at Veridian.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, on the IT team — a chance to get a first sense of his day-to-day priorities.
Keep the weekly rhythm going with Neta and raise anything that needs attention.
A direct working relationship with Yael as one of the leaders in your portfolio — separate from the skip-level conversation you already had.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, on the Legal team — a first sense of what he'll come to you for.
One of the leaders in your portfolio, leading Business Operations — a chance to get a first sense of her priorities.
A short sync with Neta to stay in step and catch anything early.
Your weekly touchpoint with Neta — stay aligned and clear out any blockers.

internalGaps: human_buddy_email is not set for this hire. Office tour used a fallback guide (Tal Harari, teammate at the same Tel Aviv office) rather than the buddy.

hrbp_email is not set for this employee, so no 'meeting with your HRBP' item exists in this plan. Plausibly intentional since she's part of the HRBP function herself, but that's not confirmed in the data - flagged rather than assumed.

The Teams catalog has no entry for 'People Partners' - team mission and core_tools are unknown. The team-member intros (Rachel Cooper, Tal Harari) and the department overview used real employee-table records and department.mission/primary_kpis directly instead.
company_overview only has basic summary fields (name, category, employee count, offices) - no product description, ICP, or business-model detail exists anywhere in the source data.
DEMO ASSUMPTION (see prompts/process-expert.md and README.md): business-track LMS sessions 3-6 have no real source data behind them - descriptions are topical only.
No manager intake was supplied for this run, so no Professional Mentor data exists - no mentor item was written, and this is a pipeline limitation for this test run, not a fact about the employee.

Her 9-person portfolio is scheduled as 9 separate individual 1:1s across weeks 3-6, not a group session - the CEO, CPO and CRO are never bundled into a shared session with each other or with the Finance/IT/Legal/Ops managers in her portfolio.
This plan does not include applied 'doing' work tickets (out of scope by design for this pipeline).
